name: durable-spec-states-what-is
body:
**A durable spec states what is / what needs to be — never the past.** A spec node describes the target reality (or, where a plan is needed, what must become true). It is not a record of changes, attempts, rejections, or reconciliations: git history describes the past, the durable spec describes what is. Two rules govern every durable spec statement. **(a) State what is.** A spec node states target truth: what is, or what needs to become true. **(b) State timeless truth.** A spec node states a truth that holds at every moment; time-relative wording that ages — `today`, `now`, `currently`, `no longer`, `was`, `previously` — belongs nowhere in the spec, because a statement true only at one moment is either the target truth or it belongs in git history. This applies across the whole distributed agent suite APG ships — `opencode-suite/agents/*.md`, embedded into the `apg` binary via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` into `~/.opencode/agents/`.

WRITER RULES — `spec-writer`, `plan-writer`, `codebase-navigator`:
- (a) Author target truth only. A replaced statement is updated or removed, never annotated as replaced, corrected, reconciled, or historical.
- (b) Author timeless wording only. Time-relative wording that ages — `today`, `now`, `currently`, `no longer`, `was`, `previously` — is a blocked form, because a statement true only at one moment is either the target truth or it belongs in git history; write the statement as what is.
- Do not author rejected alternatives, change-logs, or decision / reconciliation / correction / provenance notes. A `note` node exists ONLY to deepen the understanding of what is — a definition, an invariant, or rationale for the design as it is — never to record a replacement, a decision against something, or a source-statement / inconsistency / resolution trail.
- A `note` never details another `note`. A note about a note is commentary on the spec's history and ages by definition; a `note` details only the non-note node or code it deepens (the binary refuses a `Note`→`Note` `details` edge at write time).
- Materializing a source spec, or reconciling the spec to an implementation, rewrites the authored nodes to what is; it leaves no provenance trail and no per-change note.

REVIEWER RULES — `spec-review`, `plan-review`, `implementation-phase-reviewer`:
- (a) Review every changed spec node against these principles.
- (b) Treat time-relative wording that ages — `today`, `now`, `currently`, `no longer`, `was`, `previously` — as BLOCKING history content: a statement true only at one moment is either the target truth or it belongs in git history, and the required fix is to rewrite the wording as what is.
- History content in a spec node is a BLOCKING finding: replaced/past-state wording, a change-log, a rejected alternative, a decision/reconciliation/correction/provenance note, a `Note`→`Note` `details` attempt, or a note whose content is really about another note or a past state rather than what is. Attach Feedback on the offending node.
- The required fix is to DELETE or REWRITE the offending content to what is — never to add a note, re-tag it, or annotate it.

ACCEPTANCE (prompt-only; assessed by review of the edited prompt files; no seeded global constraint, no binary change, no lint):
- `opencode-suite/agents/spec-writer.md`, `plan-writer.md`, and `codebase-navigator.md` state the writer rules, both (a) author target truth only and (b) author timeless wording only: a replaced statement is updated or removed, never annotated; no time-relative wording that ages — `today`, `now`, `currently`, `no longer`, `was`, `previously` — because a statement true only at one moment is either the target truth or it belongs in git history; no rejected alternatives, change-logs, or decision/reconciliation/correction/provenance notes; a `note` deepens understanding of what is only and never details another `note`.
- `opencode-suite/agents/spec-review.md`, `plan-review.md`, and `implementation-phase-reviewer.md` state the reviewer rules, both (a) and (b): review every changed spec node against the principles; raise blocking feedback on history content — time-relative wording that ages (`today`, `now`, `currently`, `no longer`, `was`, `previously`) as well as replaced/past-state wording, a `Note`→`Note` `details` attempt, or a note whose content is about another note or a past state; the fix is delete/rewrite, never annotate.
- The suite's `note` node type is defined only as deepening the understanding of what is, and no prompt instructs or expects a per-change provenance/decision/reconciliation note.
